newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: S.Lanka must change attitude to work, says minister.
newsitem.headline: S.Lanka must change attitude to work, says minister.

text.p: Sri Lankans need to change their attitude to work if their country is to compete with its neighbours, a minister, industrialists and consultants said.

Deputy Minister for Industrial Development Atula Nimalasiri Jayasinhe told a seminar late on Wednesday the Indian Ocean island's productivity had to improve radically with the population working more efficiently and effectively.

"If we look at some of our neighbours like Singapore and Malaysia, we see nations that are prospering because they learned to be more competitive and productive. These are lessons we must learn," Jayasinhe said.
"We have a long way to go."
Sri Lanka recently launched a 10-year campaign to boost productivity in the Indian Ocean island, which consultants say lags most of its Asian competitors.

Sunil Wijesinha, consultant to the Ministry of Industrial Development, told the seminar that Sri Lanka's productivity -- gross domestic product (GDP) divided by the size of the labour force -- was $1,776 in 1993.
This was the third lowest in a study of 10 Asian countries.
Japan came top in the survey with a productivity of $27,857, with Singapore second at $20,425. Bottom in the survey was Pakistan with a productivity of $1,250.
He said Sri Lankans had to learn to use time efficiently.
"People here think that time is unlimited, whereas Westerners think of time as a limited resource," he said. "Most people in Sri Lanka also think that change spells trouble."
But Wijesinha said Sri Lanka could compete effectively under the right conditions, because the country's literacy rate was very high at 89.3 percent.

"Given the right environment, Sri Lankans are as productive as anybody else," he said. "Some foreign investors...have said that the productive level of Sri Lankan factories is higher or equal to factories in their home countries."
